chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, son of Yahya, from Ahmad, son of Muhammad, son of Isa, from Abd al-Rahman, son of Hammaad, from Muhammad, son of Is'haq, from Muhammad, son of al-Fayz, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When one of us falls ill, the healers order us to go on a diet.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'But we, the People of the Household, do not abstain except from dates, and we cure ourselves with apples and cold water.' I said: 'And why do you abstain from dates?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'Because the Prophet of Allah kept Ali (peace be upon him) away from it during his illness.'
ai.seo_question: Why do the Ahl al-Bayt avoid dates and prefer apples and cold water for healing?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific dietary regimen for the Ahl al-Bayt, avoiding dates while favoring apples and cold water, a practice rooted in the precedent of the Prophet restricting Ali during his illness. This hadith highlights the distinct medical and spiritual traditions of the Imams, emphasizing that their health practices are not merely empirical but derived from prophetic authority and divine wisdom. It serves as a practical example of how the Ahl al-Bayt’s unique status influences their approach to physical well-being and disease prevention.
